function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "is chrome is installed". They want to check if Chrome is installed. We can use the provided function to run a command. On Windows, we can check if Chrome is installed by checking the existence of chrome.exe in Program Files or by querying registry. But we can just try to run "where chrome" or "where chrome.exe" to see if it's found. Or "where google-chrome" on Windows? Actually Chrome is usually installed at "C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" or "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe". We can run "where chrome" which will search PATH. But Chrome might not be in PATH. Alternatively, we can check registry: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\chrome.exe. But easier: try to run "where chrome.exe" and see if it returns path. If not found, maybe not installed.

We can use the function to run "where chrome.exe". Let's do that.
